query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: A single thermal processing intervention—rapid thermal annealing (RTA)—applied to an equiatomic FeCoNi high-entropy alloy can induce microstructural strain and subtle chemical ordering (e.g., formation of low‐symmetry, potentially L10-like domains) that increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy, thereby raising coercivity compared to the untreated fcc baseline.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy forming a single fcc phase with high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
generation.intervention: Apply a rapid thermal annealing (RTA) treatment with controlled temperature and time parameters.
generation.conditions: The treatment should be conducted while maintaining the equiatomic multicomponent composition and a configurational entropy of at least 1.0R, with processing conditions chosen to induce strain and local ordering without causing phase separation or a significant loss in configurational disorder.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of strain-induced low-symmetry regions (such as annealing twins or short-range ordered domains reminiscent of L10-type ordering) within the overall high-entropy fcc matrix that serve as effective domain wall pinning sites.
generation.mechanism: The RTA process promotes microstructural reconfiguration by creating local strain and chemical ordering that reduce the high symmetry of the original fcc lattice. This reduced symmetry, combined with enhanced domain wall pinning at newly created microstructural features, increases the magnetocrystalline anisotropy and hence the coercive field.
generation.predicted_outcome: After RTA treatment, the FeCoNi-based HEA will display an increased coercivity relative to the untreated fcc baseline, while still preserving a high saturation magnetization and an overall single-phase high-entropy structure.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic FeCoNi-based HEA in the fcc phase with low coercivity.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies as long as the RTA parameters do not induce extensive phase decomposition or ordering that would drop the configurational entropy well below 1.0R. The results are expected to hold for processing conditions that promote moderate strain and subtle chemical ordering without triggering a full phase transition to a non-HEA structure.
generation.uncertainty: The precise RTA temperature, time, and cooling rate required to optimize the strain-induced ordering and coercivity increase are not yet determined and may require fine tuning to avoid compromising the high-entropy phase.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare equiatomic FeCoNi HEA samples and divide them into sets subject to different RTA conditions (varying temperature, time, and cooling rates). Use X-ray diffraction (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to characterize any induced structural changes (e.g., emergence of low-symmetry regions, grain boundary evolution). Measure magnetic properties with vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM) to obtain hysteresis loops. Compare the coercivity of RTA-treated samples to that of untreated baseline samples.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If none of the RTA-treated samples show a statistically significant increase in coercivity relative to the untreated fcc baseline, or if the treatment causes a loss of the single-phase high-entropy structure (i.e., a configurational entropy drop below 1.0R or unwanted phase separation), then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.
